The United States on Tuesday carried out several attacks on Iran’s southern Island of Qeshm, located in the Strait of Hormuz, a local Iranian official said. “The American attack on locations on Qeshm island caused no damage to residential, commercial, or infrastructural areas,” said Ahmad Nafisi, deputy provincial governor of the southern province of Hormozgan, quoted by the official IRNA news agency. “The situation on Qeshm island is under control, and all relief, service, and executive agencies are on full alert,” he added. “The sounds of five to six explosions were heard on Qeshm on Tuesday evening,” IRNA said. Earlier in the day Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they had launched a drone attack targeting a radar system in Bahrain operated by the United States. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain,” the Guards’ Sepah news website said. It added that the attack was in response to the “repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones”. Since the outbreak of the Middle East war in late February, Tehran has attempted to restrict traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use only routes authorised by the Islamic republic. It has regularly targeted ships that transit without its authorisation. The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil supplies. In recent weeks, Tehran has made multiple announcements saying ships have caught fire in the strait, often claiming they struck mines. On Tuesday, the Iranian armed forces said three oil tankers struck naval mines while attempting to transit Hormuz. The US military recently said it had cleared all mines from the main routes through the waterway. US Central Command, which oversees US military operations in the region, said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.
